about.title: Dreamer
about.subtitle: A tool for Jungian dreamwork and inner reflection
about.disclaimer: This project is intended for personal reflection and educational exploration. It is not a substitute for psychotherapy or professional mental health care.

jung.heading: What is Jungian Dreamwork?
jung.p1: Carl Jung believed that dreams are not random noise, but meaningful communications from the unconscious psyche. Where Freud focused on repressed wishes, Jung saw dreams as compensatory messages — the unconscious showing us what our waking mind overlooks, neglects, or cannot yet integrate.
jung.p2: Central to Jung's framework are a few core ideas. The <accent>shadow</accent> holds qualities we deny in ourselves — both dark and light. The <accent>anima / animus</accent> represents the contrasexual inner figure that mediates between the ego and the deeper unconscious. The <accent>Self</accent> is the organising centre of the whole psyche, often appearing in dreams as a figure of authority, a wise elder, or a numinous symbol. Through dreamwork, we begin to recognise these figures not as strangers, but as parts of ourselves seeking acknowledgement.
jung.p3: Jung's method of <accent>amplification</accent> asks the dreamer to circle a symbol outward — associating it with personal memories, cultural parallels, and archetypal themes — rather than reducing it to a single fixed meaning. The goal is not a definitive answer but a richer dialogue with the unconscious.

innerWork.heading: Robert A. Johnson's Inner Work
innerWork.p1: Analyst Robert A. Johnson distilled Jung's approach into a four-step practice in his book Inner Work. First, gather your associations — what does each image bring to mind from your own life? Second, connect the dream to your inner life — treat every figure as an aspect of your own psyche rather than as a commentary on other people. Third, interpret — form tentative hypotheses and hold them lightly. Fourth, make the insight concrete through a small ritual or lived act that honours what the dream asked of you.
innerWork.p2: Johnson insists that interpretations are always provisional. No symbol has a fixed universal meaning. The dreamer's own associations come first, and the most valuable dreamwork ends not in a clever reading but in a modest, embodied change.

howItWorks.heading: How This App Works
howItWorks.intro: Dreamer walks you through Johnson's four steps as a structured session:

record.title: Record
record.description: Write your dream in free text. The app parses it into characters, symbols, settings, emotions, and narrative shifts so nothing gets lost.

associate.title: Associate
associate.description: For each element, you supply your own personal associations. The app never overrides these with dictionary definitions.

interpret.title: Interpret
interpret.description: Using your dream and associations, the AI generates several clearly labelled hypotheses — compensation, shadow, anima/animus, archetypal, and individuation. Each is a question to sit with, not a verdict.

integrate.title: Integrate
integrate.description: The app suggests a small, concrete act to bring the dream's insight into waking life — in the spirit of Johnson's ritual step.

howItWorks.footnote: All interpretations are framed as hypotheses. Your associations take precedence over any AI suggestion. The app is designed for personal reflection — it makes no diagnostic or therapeutic claims, and your data stays private.
